Robotic system · 2022–2025

OpenChessRobot

An open-source chess robot for studying how people interact with a system that sees, acts and explains.

PaperCode

The problem

To study interaction with an intelligent robot, people need a system they can actually use. Chess supplies a rich but verifiable setting: the board state, legal moves and engine evaluation can be checked independently of the robot’s spoken explanation.

What I built

The system combines a Franka Panda arm, ZED2 camera, learned piece recognition, chess-state validation, Stockfish, MoveIt motion planning and LLM-generated spoken commentary. ROS connects the modules, and an open hardware design includes a gripper adapted to the chess pieces.

Recognition alone is insufficient. The perceived board is checked against chess rules and the previous state before execution. An illegal state triggers another observation from a shifted camera pose. The language model provides commentary; Stockfish supplies the move decision.

What the evaluation showed

The study combined component evaluation, a 597-person scenario survey and a FIDE Master case study. The robot provided a reproducible interaction platform, while the expert assessment exposed a gap between fluent commentary and strategic depth.

Research takeaway: a system can appear coherent at the interface while one part of its reasoning remains shallow. Evaluation needs to distinguish perception, action and explanation quality.

Where this leads

This platform motivates my next question: can a robot turn a failure into a testable diagnosis, then use the evidence to select a better intervention?
